observations: Photo 0 and 1: a large monocrystalline, half-cut-cell solar panel with silver aluminum frame, photographed upright in a cluttered shop/warehouse setting in Lagos, Nigeria (per photo timestamp/location overlay).
Photo 2 and 3: reverse side of a panel, white backsheet, junction box with two MC4-style connector cables, and a small printed specification label near the junction box.
The specification label in photo 3 is visible but the text (brand, model, wattage, voltage) is too small/blurry to read.
Watermark 'NETWORK SOLAR VENTURES' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' appear on photos 1-3; this is the seller's branding, not the panel manufacturer's.
Background shows coils of cable, other panel stacks, and bystanders, consistent with a solar equipment shop.
Location tag says Lagos, Nigeria, though the buyer's market is Oyo - likely the seller's shop location, not necessarily a red flag by itself.

claims.claim: Seller intro: 'Thank you for contacting Network Solar venture... We deal...' (message cut off, no specific product claims made)
claims.evidence: No specific claim about this item's condition, wattage, or performance is stated in the text.

claims.claim: Implied: item is new/unused solar panel
claims.evidence: Photos show a clean, apparently unused panel with protective packaging materials nearby (photo 3), but no invoice, box label, or seller statement confirming 'new' condition.

risks.risk: Wattage and electrical specifications (Wp, Voc, Isc) are unknown, which drives most of a solar panel's price.
risks.proof: A clear, well-lit close-up photo of the specification sticker/label visible in photo 3, fully legible.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this; wattage is the primary price determinant for solar panels

risks.risk: Panel could be used/refurbished rather than new, affecting value significantly.
risks.proof: Close-up of any production date stamp, original manufacturer box, or seller statement with proof of purchase/invoice.

risks.risk: Cell or frame micro-cracks, hotspots, or hidden damage not visible in static photos.
risks.proof: A short video or multi-angle shots in direct sunlight showing uniform cell color, plus an IV-curve/output test with a multimeter under sun.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not verified working, i.e., functional condition unproven

risks.risk: Junction box and MC4 connectors could be damaged or non-OEM, affecting safety/durability.
risks.proof: Close-up of junction box seal and connector pins.

risks.risk: Brand/manufacturer unknown; could be an unbranded or lesser-known OEM panel, which affects resale and warranty value.
risks.proof: Legible shot of brand name/logo on frame or label.

proof_requests: Clear, in-focus close-up of the specification label on the back of the panel (wattage, model, Voc, Isc, brand).
Any manufacturer box, invoice, or warranty card showing brand and purchase date.
Daylight video showing panel connected to a load/meter to confirm power output.
Close-up of cell surface and frame corners for crack/damage check.
response.reason: The item is clearly a monocrystalline half-cut solar panel, but the wattage/spec label that sets its price class is unreadable in all photos, so even a worst-case price cannot be assigned without it.
